item.title: I've been waiting...
item.content:encoded:
I've been waiting so long. After hearing a stand-up routine by Dane Cook involving "Kool" years ago I had hoped to happen upon a serious situation where a person says, "Oh no" followed by the inevitable "Oh Yeah" and destruction. I think this is as close as I'm getting and I love it.

I generally don't like "J's" or anything about them but… Upvoted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Ehhhh…. Gonna have to be a down vote this time. The joke is basically the same as the SCP told as a tale. It doesn't really add to the joke and honestly the tale could be added to any fiction site and as long as there was a TV savvy audience people would get the joke. On it's own it's not really strong enough but I could easily see this being part of some larger work that would garner an upvote (Containment Breach-J eh?)

item.title: I have to wonder...
item.content:encoded: Why does the 1344-J instance, one or more than one, follow this poor woman? Has it chosen her as its victim to torment by tearing her life apart, does it feed on misery and sheer panic? Or does she shine as a beacon to all instances of 1344-J, destined to have a horde of them following her to the ends of the earth. Does this in fact make her the bringer of the end times?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I think you're missing the more horrifying implication. What if there's more than one?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Not feeling it; the whole point of 1344-J is that he's a pitcher plant disguised as the Kool-Aid Man. Kool-Aid Man wouldn't crash an adult's insurance meeting; he's supposed to crash events that involve kids, like school assemblies or boring birthday parties.
